sections.title: Eligibility and preparation
sections.text:
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
Eligible in principle after a mathematics bachelor's or equivalent preparation; the catalog ordinarily requires a
3.0 undergraduate GPA for work beyond the first 60 semester/90 quarter credits. Proof-based algebra and
analysis preparation is important. International applicants can enter the PhD and receive assistantships. F1
status is not permanent residence; an old departmental instruction asking every noncitizen for a resident-alien
number does not fit an F1 applicant, so use the current portal's actual immigration category and ask
admissions if that legacy field appears. [s1] [s3] [s4]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Prepare the UF/ApplyWeb application, transcripts, required CV and mathematics statement; request all three
references before final submission, because UF says references cannot be added or deleted after submission.
Send any required official English scores early. Apply for Mathematics PhD and indicate funding interest. Do
not enter a resident-alien number if you do not have one. No advance supervisor agreement is published. [s1]
[s2] [s3]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
No prior supervisor agreement is listed. For application logistics, use math-gradapps@ufl.edu. Faculty below
are potential intellectual fits, not confirmed 2027 recruiters. A short inquiry grounded in a recent paper is
appropriate where there is a specific research connection. [s1] [s14]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
UF uses ApplyWeb/CollegeNET for the application and MyAdmissions for status. A UFID can take approximately
24-48 hours to appear. Follow the checklist; an 'under review' label alone does not establish that every item is
missing or complete. Request all referees before final submission and use the electronic recommendation
status page. International-center visa documentation follows admission. [s2] [s3] [s11] [s12]
Cycle verification [Standing rule]
Most mathematics admissions and funding pages are standing/undated, so the December 2026 date is the
application of a recurring December 1 rule rather than an explicit fall-2027 announcement. The revised TOEFL
policy explicitly applies from spring 2027. The payroll calendar covers 2026-27 but does not by itself establish
a 2027 stipend. [s1] [s3] [s29]

sections.title: Deadlines by stage
sections.text:
Academic application [Standing rule]
December 1 preceding fall entry is the standing mathematics deadline, hence December 1, 2026 for fall 2027
by interpretation of the recurring rule; the checked page does not explicitly label the 2027 cycle or state a
clock/time zone. Fall admission only. Late files may be considered if time and places permit, not a guaranteed
extension. [s1]
Funding consideration [Standing rule]
December 1 is the department's complete-file admission and financial-support consideration deadline. No
separate 2027 fellowship nomination deadline was published in the sources checked. [s1] [s5]
Reference receipt [Standing rule]
All three recommendations should be received by the December 1 complete-application deadline. No
mathematics-specific late-reference grace period is published. Send requests before submitting the
application. [s1] [s2]
Test-score receipt [Standing rule]
Required scores belong in the complete file by December 1. The department recommends October testing;
that is planning guidance rather than a separate hard deadline. UF advises allowing 2-4 weeks for official
electronic score processing. ETS institution code 5812; use the University of Florida IELTS electronic delivery
listing. [s1] [s3]
Supporting documents [Standing rule]
Application-stage transcripts, CV, statement and other required materials are due with the complete December
1 file. After admission, official academic records must be received by the end of the first enrollment term;
official test results must meet the enrollment requirement. The later official-record deadline does not excuse
missing application uploads. [s1] [s2] [s3]
Accepting an offer [Unresolved]
A mathematics-specific fall-2027 offer acceptance deadline was not established. Other UF departments' April
15 statements do not establish the mathematics rule; use the individual funding/admission letter and reconfirm
the 2027 policy. [s1] [s5]

sections.title: English and GRE
sections.text:
English requirement [Conflict]
For spring 2027 onward, central international admissions lists TOEFL 4.5 overall with at least 4 in each section
on the revised scale; IELTS Academic 6.5 or completion of the UF English Language Institute is also accepted.
The graduate catalog still presents the older TOEFL 80 minimum. Do not combine multiple tests using MyBest.
Admission exemption and teaching certification are separate. [s3] [s4] [s8]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
A completed US degree, or at least one academic year in a US degree program, can meet the published
admissions English exemption, subject to departmental discretion; John's UChicago attendance should qualify
if documented. A US bachelor's does not by itself waive UF's separate oral-English requirement for a
nonexempt international TA. Current TA minimums include TOEFL speaking 4.5, IELTS speaking 7 or SPEAK 45;
middle scores require EAP 5836 during the first teaching semester. Summer teaching requires the higher
direct-clearance threshold because EAP is unavailable then: TOEFL speaking 6 plus listening 4.5, IELTS
speaking 8.5 or SPEAK 55. UF's country exemptions must be checked against actual nationality, which is
unspecified here. [s1] [s3] [s8]
GRE General [Standing rule]
Recommended but optional in the mathematics application; not a published mandatory requirement. Confirm
the 2027 portal has not changed the standing policy. [s1]

GRE Mathematics [Standing rule]
Mathematics Subject GRE is recommended but optional. No published mandatory minimum was found. [s1]

sections.title: Academic records
sections.text:
Transcripts and degree records [Standing rule]
Submit academic records from every postsecondary institution. Application uploads should be scans of official
transcripts showing the institution, applicant, coursework, grades and official markings rather than screenshots
of a student grade portal. Include awarded degree certificates and certified literal English translations where
applicable. NACES evaluation is an optional route for some foreign records, not a requirement for a UChicago
bachelor's. After admission, official records must arrive institution-direct or in an accepted sealed form by the
end of the first enrolled term; approved certified copies may be used for irreplaceable documents. [s2] [s3]
Mathematics-course list [Unresolved]
A separate mathematics-course list is not stated on the public mathematics checklist. Transcripts and the
mathematical-background statement provide course preparation; verify whether the live application adds a
structured course field. [s1]
Course descriptions [Unresolved]
No separately required course descriptions or syllabi were identified. Obtain a specific request before assuming
they are needed. [s1]

sections.title: Recommendation letters
sections.text:
Number and type [Standing rule]
Three recommendations are required. The department wants at least two from instructors familiar with the
applicant's performance in proof-based mathematics courses. [s1]
Scholarship references [Unresolved]
No additional reference count or separate scholarship referee questionnaire was established for the ordinary
mathematics assistantship, Grinter nomination or McNair route. Check any invitation-specific nomination
instructions; a missing public requirement is not a waiver. [s1] [s9] [s10]
What sends the invitation [Standing rule]
ApplyWeb sends an electronic invitation when the applicant uses the reference-request submission control;
merely typing a referee's contact information is not the documented trigger. UF requires reference requests to
be arranged before final submission. [s2] [s11]
Before versus after submission [Standing rule]
Requests can be sent before submitting the application; they are not held automatically until final submission.
UF warns that references cannot be added or deleted after the application has been submitted. Writer
submissions may arrive separately, but no late-letter review guarantee is published. [s2] [s11]
Receipt confirmation [Standing rule]
ApplyWeb's activity/status view reports completed electronic recommendations. An offline letter may not
appear there; ask the department whether an alternative delivery method is accepted and recorded. [s12]
Updating and reusing letters [Standing rule]
ApplyWeb documents a writer-side revision function before the associated application is finally submitted; after
that point, contact support/admissions for correction. UF's applicant-side add/delete restriction still applies.
Reusing letters across application cycles or other UF programs was not established. [s2] [s13]

sections.title: Written materials
sections.text:
Academic CV / resume [Standing rule]
CV/resume is required as an attachment. Central instructions call for post-high-school education and
employment and relevant ongoing international affiliations, research and funding information. A
mathematics-specific page/word limit, file type, font or margin rule was not publicly established; verify the
upload slot before drafting the final file. [s2]
Statement of purpose [Standing rule]
Required mathematics statement: describe your mathematical background and possible areas of interest
(faithful paraphrase; use the linked page and live prompt for the exact wording). No public mathematics
word/page limit, formatting rule or separate 2027 prompt was established. [s1]
Personal / background statement [Unresolved]
No separate mathematics personal/background essay is listed publicly. Check the current UF application for
any central short answer before final submission. [s1] [s2]
Research-interest statement [Standing rule]
Possible mathematical research interests belong in the required mathematics statement. A separate
research-interest document is not listed publicly. [s1]
Research proposal [Unresolved]
A formal research proposal is not listed on the public mathematics application checklist. A supervisor-specific
request would need separate confirmation. [s1]
Writing sample / thesis / research summary [Unresolved]
A thesis, paper or writing sample is not listed as a required mathematics upload. No public instruction
established whether optional work should be linked or uploaded; do not assume an unsolicited manuscript will
be read. [s1]
Publications list [Unresolved]
A separate publication list is not listed publicly; relevant research/publications can be described in the CV and
statement. Optional paper-upload versus link policy remains unverified. [s1] [s2]
Course-list document [Unresolved]
No separate mathematics-course-list document or prompt was found. Confirm structured course questions in
the active application. [s1]
Scholarship essays [Unresolved]
Grinter is a departmental nomination route; public instructions do not expose all internal Canvas nomination
prompts. McNair is restricted to qualifying prior program participants, with the next cycle's instructions
requiring separate confirmation. Exact scholarship essays, limits and formatting for a fall-2027 nominee were
not established. [s9] [s10]
Other short answers / materials [Unresolved]
No other mathematics-specific written attachment was identified. UF's central application may require
immigration, academic-history or background explanations based on answers; inspect all conditional fields
before drafting. [s1] [s2]

sections.title: Funding and fees
sections.text:
Amount and coverage [Prior cycle]
A guaranteed mathematics fall-2027 annual stipend was not published. UF HR's October 1, 2024 minimum
schedule lists $20,600 for a 9-month 0.50-FTE appointment and $27,467 for a 12-month 0.50-FTE
appointment; these are institutional minimums for those appointment terms, not a 2027 mathematics offer.
Mathematics describes tuition waiver and assistantship support, but students retain some fees; its
approximate $680 per 9-credit semester fee estimate is undated and must be refreshed. GatorGradCare
provides qualifying graduate-employee health coverage; exact 2027 deductions and dependent costs require
the offer/benefit schedule. [s5] [s6] [s7] [s29]
Years of support [Standing rule]
The mathematics guide describes support for up to five years, subject to satisfactory academic and teaching
progress and annual renewal. Summer support is often available but is not guaranteed. Ask whether the offer
covers 9, 11 or 12 months and how summers are funded. [s5]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
International PhD students are eligible for departmental assistantships, subject to employment eligibility and
oral-English certification for teaching. The admission English waiver does not settle TA eligibility. Exact
nonresident-tuition coverage and any remaining fees should be stated in the offer; do not equate tuition
remission with all charges being paid. [s1] [s5] [s8]
Conditions and duties [Conflict]
Maintain satisfactory progress, typically at least a 3.0 graduate GPA and required registration (the guide
specifies at least 9 credits in fall/spring). Teaching and English certification matter; the PhD includes teaching
experience. The admissions page describes half-time/20-hour assistantships with roughly 3-4 contact hours,
while the funding guide describes a one-third-time arrangement: resolve the appointment fraction in writing.
F1 academic-term employment is normally limited to the permitted half-time load. GatorGradCare eligibility
begins at a qualifying 0.25 FTE appointment; employee-only coverage is automatic under the January 2025
policy, dependents need timely enrollment, and a separate student-health-insurance waiver must be submitted
each term to avoid duplicate student-plan charges. [s1] [s5] [s6] [s7] [s8]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
Indicate financial-support interest in the mathematics application. Ordinary support is considered with
admission; Grinter and other institutional fellowships use departmental nomination. No universally required
separate scholarship essay or reference was established publicly. [s1] [s5] [s9]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
Grinter provides a published $2,000-$4,000 supplement for up to three PhD years; confirm payment period,
international eligibility and 2027 nomination rules. The McNair route is for qualifying former McNair participants
and lists $13,000 plus tuition/fees for the first two years, with additional assistantship support possible; John's
eligibility cannot be inferred. Mathematics also mentions Alumni fellowships, summer appointments, CAM and
CLAS research/travel support; award amounts and open calls vary. No external citizenship-restricted award
should be assumed available solely because John holds F1 status. [s5] [s9] [s10]
Application fee [Standing rule]
$30 nonrefundable application fee. [s1] [s2]
Fee waiver [Standing rule]
Both central admissions and the mathematics instructions say the application fee cannot be waived. Do not
rely on another institution's financial-need waiver or assume F1 eligibility. [s1] [s2]

text:
University of Florida
United States · Mathematics PhD
Rank verified separately
Eligibility and preparation · Deadlines by stage · English and GRE · Academic records · Recommendation letters · Written
materials · Funding and fees · Conflicts and remaining checks · Faculty · Sources
Pay attention to
• December 1 is a standing rule, not an explicitly dated fall-2027 announcement.
• UChicago may waive admission English testing; it does not automatically waive UF international-TA
oral-English certification.
• Arrange all reference requests before final submission; UF limits later add/delete changes.
• No fee waiver is published; a mathematics fall-2027 stipend remains unconfirmed.
• Resolve the conflicting assistantship fractions and obtain exact summer and fee terms.
• Complete the separate student-health-insurance waiver each term if using GatorGradCare.
Eligibility and preparation
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
Eligible in principle after a mathematics bachelor's or equivalent preparation; the catalog ordinarily requires a
3.0 undergraduate GPA for work beyond the first 60 semester/90 quarter credits. Proof-based algebra and
analysis preparation is important. International applicants can enter the PhD and receive assistantships. F1
status is not permanent residence; an old departmental instruction asking every noncitizen for a resident-alien
number does not fit an F1 applicant, so use the current portal's actual immigration category and ask
admissions if that legacy field appears. [s1] [s3] [s4]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Prepare the UF/ApplyWeb application, transcripts, required CV and mathematics statement; request all three
references before final submission, because UF says references cannot be added or deleted after submission.
Send any required official English scores early. Apply for Mathematics PhD and indicate funding interest. Do
not enter a resident-alien number if you do not have one. No advance supervisor agreement is published. [s1]
[s2] [s3]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
No prior supervisor agreement is listed. For application logistics, use math-gradapps@ufl.edu. Faculty below
are potential intellectual fits, not confirmed 2027 recruiters. A short inquiry grounded in a recent paper is
appropriate where there is a specific research connection. [s1] [s14]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
UF uses ApplyWeb/CollegeNET for the application and MyAdmissions for status. A UFID can take approximately
24-48 hours to appear. Follow the checklist; an 'under review' label alone does not establish that every item is
missing or complete. Request all referees before final submission and use the electronic recommendation
status page. International-center visa documentation follows admission. [s2] [s3] [s11] [s12]
Cycle verification [Standing rule]
Most mathematics admissions and funding pages are standing/undated, so the December 2026 date is the
application of a recurring December 1 rule rather than an explicit fall-2027 announcement. The revised TOEFL
policy explicitly applies from spring 2027. The payroll calendar covers 2026-27 but does not by itself establish
a 2027 stipend. [s1] [s3] [s29]

Deadlines by stage
Academic application [Standing rule]
December 1 preceding fall entry is the standing mathematics deadline, hence December 1, 2026 for fall 2027
by interpretation of the recurring rule; the checked page does not explicitly label the 2027 cycle or state a
clock/time zone. Fall admission only. Late files may be considered if time and places permit, not a guaranteed
extension. [s1]
Funding consideration [Standing rule]
December 1 is the department's complete-file admission and financial-support consideration deadline. No
separate 2027 fellowship nomination deadline was published in the sources checked. [s1] [s5]
Reference receipt [Standing rule]
All three recommendations should be received by the December 1 complete-application deadline. No
mathematics-specific late-reference grace period is published. Send requests before submitting the
application. [s1] [s2]
Test-score receipt [Standing rule]
Required scores belong in the complete file by December 1. The department recommends October testing;
that is planning guidance rather than a separate hard deadline. UF advises allowing 2-4 weeks for official
electronic score processing. ETS institution code 5812; use the University of Florida IELTS electronic delivery
listing. [s1] [s3]
Supporting documents [Standing rule]
Application-stage transcripts, CV, statement and other required materials are due with the complete December
1 file. After admission, official academic records must be received by the end of the first enrollment term;
official test results must meet the enrollment requirement. The later official-record deadline does not excuse
missing application uploads. [s1] [s2] [s3]
Accepting an offer [Unresolved]
A mathematics-specific fall-2027 offer acceptance deadline was not established. Other UF departments' April
15 statements do not establish the mathematics rule; use the individual funding/admission letter and reconfirm
the 2027 policy. [s1] [s5]
English and GRE
English requirement [Conflict]
For spring 2027 onward, central international admissions lists TOEFL 4.5 overall with at least 4 in each section
on the revised scale; IELTS Academic 6.5 or completion of the UF English Language Institute is also accepted.
The graduate catalog still presents the older TOEFL 80 minimum. Do not combine multiple tests using MyBest.
Admission exemption and teaching certification are separate. [s3] [s4] [s8]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
A completed US degree, or at least one academic year in a US degree program, can meet the published
admissions English exemption, subject to departmental discretion; John's UChicago attendance should qualify
if documented. A US bachelor's does not by itself waive UF's separate oral-English requirement for a
nonexempt international TA. Current TA minimums include TOEFL speaking 4.5, IELTS speaking 7 or SPEAK 45;
middle scores require EAP 5836 during the first teaching semester. Summer teaching requires the higher
direct-clearance threshold because EAP is unavailable then: TOEFL speaking 6 plus listening 4.5, IELTS
speaking 8.5 or SPEAK 55. UF's country exemptions must be checked against actual nationality, which is
unspecified here. [s1] [s3] [s8]
GRE General [Standing rule]
Recommended but optional in the mathematics application; not a published mandatory requirement. Confirm
the 2027 portal has not changed the standing policy. [s1]

GRE Mathematics [Standing rule]
Mathematics Subject GRE is recommended but optional. No published mandatory minimum was found. [s1]
Academic records
Transcripts and degree records [Standing rule]
Submit academic records from every postsecondary institution. Application uploads should be scans of official
transcripts showing the institution, applicant, coursework, grades and official markings rather than screenshots
of a student grade portal. Include awarded degree certificates and certified literal English translations where
applicable. NACES evaluation is an optional route for some foreign records, not a requirement for a UChicago
bachelor's. After admission, official records must arrive institution-direct or in an accepted sealed form by the
end of the first enrolled term; approved certified copies may be used for irreplaceable documents. [s2] [s3]
Mathematics-course list [Unresolved]
A separate mathematics-course list is not stated on the public mathematics checklist. Transcripts and the
mathematical-background statement provide course preparation; verify whether the live application adds a
structured course field. [s1]
Course descriptions [Unresolved]
No separately required course descriptions or syllabi were identified. Obtain a specific request before assuming
they are needed. [s1]
Recommendation letters
Number and type [Standing rule]
Three recommendations are required. The department wants at least two from instructors familiar with the
applicant's performance in proof-based mathematics courses. [s1]
Scholarship references [Unresolved]
No additional reference count or separate scholarship referee questionnaire was established for the ordinary
mathematics assistantship, Grinter nomination or McNair route. Check any invitation-specific nomination
instructions; a missing public requirement is not a waiver. [s1] [s9] [s10]
What sends the invitation [Standing rule]
ApplyWeb sends an electronic invitation when the applicant uses the reference-request submission control;
merely typing a referee's contact information is not the documented trigger. UF requires reference requests to
be arranged before final submission. [s2] [s11]
Before versus after submission [Standing rule]
Requests can be sent before submitting the application; they are not held automatically until final submission.
UF warns that references cannot be added or deleted after the application has been submitted. Writer
submissions may arrive separately, but no late-letter review guarantee is published. [s2] [s11]
Receipt confirmation [Standing rule]
ApplyWeb's activity/status view reports completed electronic recommendations. An offline letter may not
appear there; ask the department whether an alternative delivery method is accepted and recorded. [s12]
Updating and reusing letters [Standing rule]
ApplyWeb documents a writer-side revision function before the associated application is finally submitted; after
that point, contact support/admissions for correction. UF's applicant-side add/delete restriction still applies.
Reusing letters across application cycles or other UF programs was not established. [s2] [s13]

Written materials
Academic CV / resume [Standing rule]
CV/resume is required as an attachment. Central instructions call for post-high-school education and
employment and relevant ongoing international affiliations, research and funding information. A
mathematics-specific page/word limit, file type, font or margin rule was not publicly established; verify the
upload slot before drafting the final file. [s2]
Statement of purpose [Standing rule]
Required mathematics statement: describe your mathematical background and possible areas of interest
(faithful paraphrase; use the linked page and live prompt for the exact wording). No public mathematics
word/page limit, formatting rule or separate 2027 prompt was established. [s1]
Personal / background statement [Unresolved]
No separate mathematics personal/background essay is listed publicly. Check the current UF application for
any central short answer before final submission. [s1] [s2]
Research-interest statement [Standing rule]
Possible mathematical research interests belong in the required mathematics statement. A separate
research-interest document is not listed publicly. [s1]
Research proposal [Unresolved]
A formal research proposal is not listed on the public mathematics application checklist. A supervisor-specific
request would need separate confirmation. [s1]
Writing sample / thesis / research summary [Unresolved]
A thesis, paper or writing sample is not listed as a required mathematics upload. No public instruction
established whether optional work should be linked or uploaded; do not assume an unsolicited manuscript will
be read. [s1]
Publications list [Unresolved]
A separate publication list is not listed publicly; relevant research/publications can be described in the CV and
statement. Optional paper-upload versus link policy remains unverified. [s1] [s2]
Course-list document [Unresolved]
No separate mathematics-course-list document or prompt was found. Confirm structured course questions in
the active application. [s1]
Scholarship essays [Unresolved]
Grinter is a departmental nomination route; public instructions do not expose all internal Canvas nomination
prompts. McNair is restricted to qualifying prior program participants, with the next cycle's instructions
requiring separate confirmation. Exact scholarship essays, limits and formatting for a fall-2027 nominee were
not established. [s9] [s10]
Other short answers / materials [Unresolved]
No other mathematics-specific written attachment was identified. UF's central application may require
immigration, academic-history or background explanations based on answers; inspect all conditional fields
before drafting. [s1] [s2]

Funding and fees
Amount and coverage [Prior cycle]
A guaranteed mathematics fall-2027 annual stipend was not published. UF HR's October 1, 2024 minimum
schedule lists $20,600 for a 9-month 0.50-FTE appointment and $27,467 for a 12-month 0.50-FTE
appointment; these are institutional minimums for those appointment terms, not a 2027 mathematics offer.
Mathematics describes tuition waiver and assistantship support, but students retain some fees; its
approximate $680 per 9-credit semester fee estimate is undated and must be refreshed. GatorGradCare
provides qualifying graduate-employee health coverage; exact 2027 deductions and dependent costs require
the offer/benefit schedule. [s5] [s6] [s7] [s29]
Years of support [Standing rule]
The mathematics guide describes support for up to five years, subject to satisfactory academic and teaching
progress and annual renewal. Summer support is often available but is not guaranteed. Ask whether the offer
covers 9, 11 or 12 months and how summers are funded. [s5]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
International PhD students are eligible for departmental assistantships, subject to employment eligibility and
oral-English certification for teaching. The admission English waiver does not settle TA eligibility. Exact
nonresident-tuition coverage and any remaining fees should be stated in the offer; do not equate tuition
remission with all charges being paid. [s1] [s5] [s8]
Conditions and duties [Conflict]
Maintain satisfactory progress, typically at least a 3.0 graduate GPA and required registration (the guide
specifies at least 9 credits in fall/spring). Teaching and English certification matter; the PhD includes teaching
experience. The admissions page describes half-time/20-hour assistantships with roughly 3-4 contact hours,
while the funding guide describes a one-third-time arrangement: resolve the appointment fraction in writing.
F1 academic-term employment is normally limited to the permitted half-time load. GatorGradCare eligibility
begins at a qualifying 0.25 FTE appointment; employee-only coverage is automatic under the January 2025
policy, dependents need timely enrollment, and a separate student-health-insurance waiver must be submitted
each term to avoid duplicate student-plan charges. [s1] [s5] [s6] [s7] [s8]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
Indicate financial-support interest in the mathematics application. Ordinary support is considered with
admission; Grinter and other institutional fellowships use departmental nomination. No universally required
separate scholarship essay or reference was established publicly. [s1] [s5] [s9]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
Grinter provides a published $2,000-$4,000 supplement for up to three PhD years; confirm payment period,
international eligibility and 2027 nomination rules. The McNair route is for qualifying former McNair participants
and lists $13,000 plus tuition/fees for the first two years, with additional assistantship support possible; John's
eligibility cannot be inferred. Mathematics also mentions Alumni fellowships, summer appointments, CAM and
CLAS research/travel support; award amounts and open calls vary. No external citizenship-restricted award
should be assumed available solely because John holds F1 status. [s5] [s9] [s10]
Application fee [Standing rule]
$30 nonrefundable application fee. [s1] [s2]
Fee waiver [Standing rule]
Both central admissions and the mathematics instructions say the application fee cannot be waived. Do not
rely on another institution's financial-need waiver or assume F1 eligibility. [s1] [s2]

Conflicts and remaining checks
Conflicting sources [Conflict]
Resolve three material differences: (1) current central TOEFL 4.5 scale versus catalog's older 80-point
minimum; (2) half-time assistantship language versus one-third-time mathematics funding-guide language; (3)
legacy blanket resident-alien-number instruction versus an F1 applicant's actual status. Admission English
exemption must not be confused with separate international-TA certification. [s1] [s3] [s4] [s5] [s8]
Checks still needed [Standing rule]
Before paying: verify the 2027 deadline clock, live statement/CV limits and conditional fields; send all three
requests before final submission; confirm the UChicago admission-English exemption and a separate TA
oral-English plan; obtain written stipend, months, appointment fraction, summer/tuition/fees/insurance terms
